previous_tier: documented (existence, material, place); inferred (start window, fence origin of the rails)
pdf_claim: Seminary Ridge barricade in the small wood in front of Schmucker Hall: fences dismantled and rails stacked into a barricade that curved through the wood, about 600 yd long (Wikipedia), held by I Corps remnants and Wainwright's artillery (20 guns Wikipedia, 22 in four batteries HistoryNet); built Jul 1 afternoon before about 16:00, overrun about 16:00-16:30; no start time, no crew list.
corrected_claim: A breastwork of rails, stumps and earth stood immediately west of the Seminary building on Jul 1. Doubleday ordered Robinson's division to intrench on its arrival and Robinson set Paul's First Brigade (16th Maine, 94th NY, 104th NY, 13th Mass., 107th Pa.) to work; the work was done between about 11:00 and about 13:00 (bounds from Baxter's arrival at 11 a.m. and the 16th Maine leaving for the right at about one o'clock), and other troops had added rails earlier in the day. Hunt counts 22 guns in four batteries on the line (16 concentrated plus Stewart's six), Wainwright counts twelve concentrated; the 20 of the PDF is not supported. Length (about 600 yd), the curve and the dismantling of a 600-yd fence line are not in any source and stay marked gaps; the form is a conflict (circular redoubt vs a line parallel to the Seminary).

sub_claims.claim: A barricade/breastwork of rails stood in front of (west of) the Seminary on Jul 1 and was used by First Corps troops.
